scenes.title: Managed Orchestration (MWAA, Cloud Composer)
scenes.narration: Managed orchestration services run Apache Airflow for you, so you author pipeline DAGs while the provider handles the schedulers, workers, and scaling.

scenes.title: Why Managed Airflow
bullets: You write DAGs in Python while the provider operates the scheduler and workers.
The environment scales workers automatically as your task load grows.
Upgrades, security patches, and integration with cloud IAM come built in.
scenes.narration: Managed Airflow lets you focus on defining pipelines as Python DAGs instead of babysitting infrastructure. The service runs and scales the scheduler and workers for you. It also handles upgrades and wires Airflow into cloud identity and logging out of the box.

scenes.title: Anatomy of a DAG
scenes.narration: An Airflow DAG describes tasks and the dependencies between them. The scheduler decides when each run should start based on your schedule. Workers then execute tasks in dependency order, and any failures trigger retries or alerts. This structure makes complex pipelines observable and repeatable.

scenes.title: A Minimal Airflow DAG
scenes.code:
from airflow import DAG
from airflow.operators.bash import BashOperator
import datetime as dt

with DAG(
    "daily_ingest",
    schedule="@daily",
    start_date=dt.datetime(2026, 1, 1),
    catchup=False,
) as dag:
    extract = BashOperator(task_id="extract", bash_command="python extract.py")
    load = BashOperator(task_id="load", bash_command="python load.py")
    extract >> load
scenes.narration: This DAG defines a simple daily pipeline. The DAG object sets the schedule and start date, and catchup is disabled so it does not backfill old runs. Two BashOperator tasks run scripts, and the bitshift operator declares that load depends on extract, guaranteeing the correct order every run.

scenes.title: Self-Hosted vs. Managed Airflow
scenes.narration: Self-hosting Airflow gives complete control but means operating the scheduler, database, and workers yourself. A managed service removes that operational burden and scales automatically. Unless you need deep customization, managed orchestration gets teams to value much faster.

scenes.text: Managed orchestration lets you focus on writing clean DAGs while the provider runs Airflow reliably — ideal for coordinating multi-step data pipelines.
scenes.narration: With managed orchestration you invest your effort in well-designed DAGs and let the provider keep Airflow running smoothly. It is the pragmatic way to coordinate complex, multi-step pipelines at scale.
